An Introduction to Chinese Tea Ceremony (Gongfu Cha)

2026-10-17 · Tea Culture

Gongfu Cha (工夫茶), literally “making tea with skill,” is a Chinese brewing tradition that uses a small teapot or gaiwan, a high leaf-to-water ratio, and many short infusions to reveal a tea’s full character.

The Essentials

  • Gaiwan or small clay pot — keeps leaf ratio high
  • Fairness pitcher (cha hai) — evens the strength across cups
  • Small tasting cups — sip and savor
  • A tea tray — catches rinse water

The Rhythm

  1. Rinse the leaves quickly with hot water (awakens the tea, discarded).
  2. Brew for 5–15 seconds for early infusions; lengthen over time.
  3. Pour into the fairness pitcher, then divide into cups.

Why It Matters

Gongfu Cha is less about formality and more about attention — to water, time and the leaf itself. It is the most rewarding way to experience fine Chinese tea.
